factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Troubleshoot external monitor connections in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft begins with Windows+P and Extend, then basic hardware isolation: remove accessories, secure or replace the cable, test the monitor on another system, try another output, and verify the graphics adapter supports the monitor count.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Troubleshoot external monitor connections in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft states that a display splitter duplicates one signal rather than creating two independent extended displays, and documents Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B, restart, driver rollback, and driver reinstall for a previously working setup.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: How to use multiple monitors in Windows
factual_notes.note: Windows 11 exposes Identify and Detect under Settings > System > Display > Multiple displays; Windows+P selects PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend, or Second screen only.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Update drivers through Device Manager in Windows
factual_notes.note: Microsoft recommends Windows Update as the normal driver source and documents rollback, automatic update, manual manufacturer packages, and reinstall through Device Manager.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Support: Keyboard shortcuts in Windows
factual_notes.note: The current shortcut reference lists Windows+P for project settings, Windows+K for Cast, and Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B for a blank or black screen.
Windows Update remains the supported path for current Windows quality and driver updates before using model-specific manufacturer support.

factual_notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Windows 11 version 24H2 known issues
factual_notes.note: The current page was checked for display-related incidents. It did not document a broad second-monitor detection incident that supersedes local monitor, cable, dock, port, projection-mode, and driver isolation.
